rule.title: State write (SSTORE) after external call violates checks-effects-interactions pattern

intent.attack_thesis: A function makes an external call (CALL/DELEGATECALL) before writing state (SSTORE), allowing the callee to re-enter and observe or manipulate stale state before it is updated.

reporting.title_template: State write after external call enables reentrancy
reporting.summary: Matches functions that perform an SSTORE after a CALL or DELEGATECALL without a reentrancy guard, violating the checks-effects-interactions pattern.
reporting.user_summary: This function writes to contract storage after making an external call. An attacker can exploit this by re-entering the function during the external call, before the state update completes, allowing them to act on stale state and potentially drain funds or corrupt accounting.
reporting.technical_summary: The detector identifies functions where an SSTORE opcode follows a CALL or DELEGATECALL in the execution path. Without a reentrancy mutex (nonReentrant modifier or equivalent), the callee can re-enter the calling contract and observe pre-update state, enabling classic reentrancy attacks on withdrawal, transfer, or accounting logic.
reporting.exploit_narrative: The attacker calls a vulnerable function that sends ETH or makes an external call before updating its internal bookkeeping. During the external call, the attacker's fallback function re-enters the vulnerable function. Because the state has not yet been updated, the contract still believes the attacker has their original balance, allowing a repeated withdrawal.
exploit_preconditions: a function performs an external CALL or DELEGATECALL before updating state via SSTORE
no reentrancy guard (nonReentrant, mutex, or equivalent) protects the function
the stale state read during re-entry controls a sensitive effect such as asset transfer or balance update
remediation_hints: follow the checks-effects-interactions pattern: update state before making external calls
add a nonReentrant modifier or mutex lock to functions with external calls
use pull-over-push payment patterns where possible

preconditions: SSTORE after external call on same path

steps.action: call victim function; callback re-enters during external call before SSTORE finalizes
steps.expected_state: state read during callback reflects pre-call values allowing duplicate execution

witness_goal.success_condition: attacker exploits stale state window between external call and SSTORE to execute privileged action twice
